notes: SR78 Container Store Decor (containerstore.com). ACCESS: curl_cffi Chrome-family impersonation, ~4-6s pacing, profile rotated per request; all fetches 200, no blocks encountered this session. DISCOVERY: the site's curated 'Featured' nav hub carries 'Trending: New & Now' (categoryId 92800, canonical /s/featured/new-now/12) -- on-page copy literally reads 'Interested in our new products? Shop The Container Store's new arrivals here!' with the hyperlink target /s/featured/whats-new/12. Fetched both URLs: byte-identical HTML (same categoryId/totalCount/canonical), confirming /whats-new is a true alias of /new-now, not a separate listing -- kept the canonical /new-now URL, noted the alias. This parent page is itself a genuine, orderable PLP (own totalCount), not just a label, so it is emitted with its own qty as well as being the parent of its genuine site-defined children. CHILDREN: the nav's category map exposes 6 real per-department New Arrivals sub-listings nested under 92800 (Kitchen, Closet, Storage, Bathroom, Travel, Home Decor), each its own /s/featured/new-now/<slug>/123 URL with its own categoryId/totalCount -- opened and verified all 6. Sum of children (161+59+66+44+27+9=366) exceeds the parent total (341); this is expected department-bucket overlap (a product can appear in more than one department's New Arrivals slice), same pattern documented in the prior Home-Decor pass and in sibling companies' Clearance/New-Arrivals breakdowns -- not an error, not deduplicated. No 'New Collection'/'New Season' editorial/lookbook page found requiring the ambiguous-Collection judgment call -- every New-Arrivals-labelled node here is a real filterable product grid with pagination, not marketing copy. No other New-Arrivals-shaped node (e.g. a plain sortField=new-arrivals view of the whole home-decor catalogue is a generic sort option on ordinary category pages, not a distinct merchandising PLP, and was excluded as an arbitrary filter per brief). No local-language variants applicable (USA/English site).
